verdict: Leads are falling and cost per lead is rising — here is what is being done.
narrative: In the last 28 days you received 121 leads at an average cost of $9.64 per lead, entirely through Meta — Google Search and local search ads have not yet gone live. Over the most recent 7 days, lead volume dropped 27% while cost per lead jumped 47%, a pattern that points to the primary Meta campaign reaching creative saturation rather than a shift in demand. Nearly all of this period's $1,166 in spend ran through a single campaign, which limits your ability to test new audiences or messaging. Ad creative is being refreshed and additional campaign lanes are being activated to distribute spend and arrest the cost-per-lead rise. Once search campaigns and landing pages are live, you will have multiple lead sources running simultaneously, which will reduce this kind of single-point exposure.

watch_item.issue: A single Meta campaign is driving 95% of spend, and lead volume is declining as cost per lead climbs — a clear signal of creative fatigue.
watch_item.fix: Ad creative is being refreshed this week and campaign structure is being broadened so spend is no longer concentrated in one placement.
